stem.text: The amount of sand in a pile at a work site changes at the rate \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} + 5 \) tons per hour for \( 0 \le t \le 20 \). At time \( t = 0 \) there are 170 tons of sand in the pile, and t is measured in hours. Using a calculator, find the time in \( 0 \le t \le 20 \) at which the amount A(t) of sand is greatest, and justify the answer. Show the setup for the calculations.

answer_key.label: The amount is greatest at t = 20, where A is 270 tons, the largest of the values of A at t = 0, at both critical points and at t = 20.

worked_solution.text: The amount is \( A(t) = 170 + \int_{0}^{t} \left(10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi s}{10} \right)} + 5\right)\,ds \), so \( A'(t) = 10 \cos{\left(\frac{\pi t}{10} \right)} + 5 \). Setting \( A'(t) = 0 \) and solving with a calculator gives \( t = 6.667 \) and \( t = 13.333 \) in the interval.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical points of an accumulation function

worked_solution.text: The candidates are the critical points and both endpoints: \( A(0) = 170 \), \( A(6.667) \approx 230.900 \), \( A(13.333) \approx 209.100 \), and \( A(20) = 170 + \int_{0}^{20} A'(s)\,ds = 270 \).
The largest candidate value is 270, at the endpoint, so the amount is greatest at \( t = 20 \) hours.
